notes: estimated_tokens = ceil(character_count / 4)
Report credits: 1 credit = 100,000 tokens.
Vendor billing: $1.00 = 100 vendor credits; 1 vendor credit = 2,500 input tokens or 500 output tokens (output costs 5x input).
Derived rates: $4.00 per 1M input tokens, $20.00 per 1M output tokens.
Waste is assumed to be 90% input tokens and 10% output tokens.
Each agent asset is assumed to be loaded 200 times per month.
Aggregate savings show a +/-20% range.
Similarity uses normalised text so whitespace-only and case-only changes are ignored.
Files under 200 characters are excluded from duplicate detection.

Scoring runs in two tiers. Tier 1 is the seven specified penalty rules with their hard caps. Tier 2 is severity scaling: for each category we measure the share of the monthly agent context budget that the category wastes, and deduct proportionally up to that category's tier 2 cap, with a category that wastes 50% or more of the budget taking the full deduction. Without tier 2 the capped rules alone could never produce a score below about 72, so the Wasteful and Critical bands would be unreachable. Both tiers are itemised in the score ledger.
Monthly agent context budget for this repository = 75,829,600 tokens (379,148 agent asset tokens x 200 runs per month).
assumptions.rates_source: Product owner supplied defaults (not yet refreshed)
assumptions.similarity_formula: similarity = Jaccard overlap of 5-word shingles on normalised text (lower-cased, whitespace collapsed, punctuation preserved)

critical.efficiency_summary_md:
# Agentic efficiency summary — agentic-crm

- Scan: `SCN-GOLDEN-critical`
- Source: github · branch `main`
- Overall efficiency score: **31 / 100**
- Verdict: **Critical** `PartialScan`
- Files parsed / skipped: 596 / 184
- Tokens analysed: 1,244,918
- Estimated monthly waste: 246,238,730 tokens (~2,462.39 credits, $1,378.95)
- Savings range: $1,103.16 to $1,654.74 per month

## Category scores

| Category | Score | Penalty | What this means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Redundancy | 0/100 | -112 | 33 groups of near-identical files and 5 repeated instruction blocks were found. |
| Token bloat | 16/100 | -84 | 9 context or memory files are over 8,000 tokens. |
| Review overhead | 47/100 | -53 | 11 review or approval steps were inferred from your instructions. |
| Agent sprawl | 48/100 | -52 | 173 agent-style files were found (108 agent roles, 25 skills). |
| Architecture inefficiency | 83/100 | -17 | 29 service directories against 39 hand written source files. |

## Top waste drivers

1. **The same instruction block is pasted into 11 files** — One block of instructions has been copied into several agent files. Only one copy is needed. The rest is paid for on every run.
   - 91,770,000 tokens/month, $513.91/month
2. **11 files are near copies of each other** — These files say almost the same thing. Every time your agents run, the same words get sent to the model more than once. Keeping one source of truth removes the repeat cost.
   - 51,437,600 tokens/month, $288.05/month
3. **11 separate review or approval steps were found** — Your instructions describe many checks before work is accepted. Each extra check means another pass over the same material, which costs time and money.
   - 26,142,550 tokens/month, $146.40/month
4. **173 agent-style files is more than this repo needs** — There are many separate agent, skill and prompt files. Each one adds instructions that have to be loaded and kept in sync. Fewer, clearer files cost less and break less often.
   - 19,545,400 tokens/month, $109.45/month
5. **Context file is very large: context.md** — This memory or context file is bigger than a healthy working budget. Large context files are re-read on every run, so most of the cost is paid again and again.
   - 7,596,200 tokens/month, $42.54/month

## Signals

- Duplicate clusters: 33
- Repeated instruction blocks: 5
- Oversized context files: 9
- Overlapping agent groups: 2
- Review stages inferred: 11
- Agent-like files: 173

## Recommended actions

| # | Action | Impact | Effort | Tokens/mo saved |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Move the shared block into one file and reference it from the others. | High | Small | 91,770,000 |
| 2 | Keep the most complete file, delete or shrink the copies, and link to the kept file instead. | High | Medium | 51,437,600 |
| 3 | Keep at most four review gates. Combine the overlapping ones into a single checklist. | High | Medium | 26,142,550 |
| 4 | Split this file into a short always-on summary plus detail files that load only when needed. | High | Medium | 7,596,200 |
| 5 | Group agents by job. Merge the ones that overlap and delete the ones nobody calls. | High | Large | 19,545,400 |
| 6 | Fold the thin services back together until each one has a clear, separate job. | High | Large | 3,791,480 |
| 7 | Keep one skill file per capability and delete the near copies. | Medium | Small | 910,500 |
| 8 | Describe the flow once in a single orchestrator file and let the agents stay simple. | Medium | Medium | 239,200 |

## Assumptions

- estimated_tokens = ceil(character_count / 4)
- Report credits: 1 credit = 100,000 tokens.
- Vendor billing: $1.00 = 100 vendor credits; 1 vendor credit = 2,500 input tokens or 500 output tokens (output costs 5x input).
- Derived rates: $4.00 per 1M input tokens, $20.00 per 1M output tokens.
- Waste is assumed to be 90% input tokens and 10% output tokens.
- Each agent asset is assumed to be loaded 200 times per month.
- Aggregate savings show a +/-20% range.
- Similarity uses normalised text so whitespace-only and case-only changes are ignored.
- Files under 200 characters are excluded from duplicate detection.
- Scoring runs in two tiers. Tier 1 is the seven specified penalty rules with their hard caps. Tier 2 is severity scaling: for each category we measure the share of the monthly agent context budget that the category wastes, and deduct proportionally up to that category's tier 2 cap, with a category that wastes 50% or more of the budget taking the full deduction. Without tier 2 the capped rules alone could never produce a score below about 72, so the Wasteful and Critical bands would be unreachable. Both tiers are itemised in the score ledger.
- Monthly agent context budget for this repository = 75,829,600 tokens (379,148 agent asset tokens x 200 runs per month).

4. **Context file is very large: context.md** — This memory or context file is bigger than a healthy working budget. Large context files are re-read on every run, so most of the cost is paid again and again.
   - 2,994,400 tokens/month, $16.77/month

   - 2,994,400 tokens/month, $16.77/month

- Repeated instruction blocks: 3
- Oversized context files: 5
- Overlapping agent groups: 3

- estimated_tokens = ceil(character_count / 4)
- Report credits: 1 credit = 100,000 tokens.

Tier 2 is severity scaling: for each category we measure the share of the monthly agent context budget that the category wastes, and deduct proportionally up to that category's tier 2 cap, with a category that wastes 50% or more of the budget taking the full deduction. Paragraph: • Scoring runs in two tiers. Tier 1 is the seven specified penalty rules with their hard caps. Tier 2 is severity scaling: for each category we measure the share of the monthly agent context budget that the category wastes, and deduct proportionally up to that category's tier 2 cap, with a category that wastes 50% or more of the budget taking the full deduction. Without tier 2 the capped rules alone could never produce a score below about 72, so the Wasteful and Critical bands would be unreachable. Both tiers are itemised in the score ledger.
Paragraph: • Monthly agent context budget for this repository = 27,878,600 tokens (139,393 agent asset tokens x 200 runs per month).
